records.text: At overseas military bases, female recruiters posing as casting directors find young women for senior personnel, and those women lack legal protection once brought onto a base.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #2 (Ep ZZGWo6oDscc)

appearances.snippet: And so what they are telling me adds up. It's tracking. What they say is, okay, think of a military base. Anywhere in the world, you have a bunch of men who do not have regular access to women. ... they tell me that they will typically send someone out who will be a woman, so think of like a Ghislaine Maxwell, to go out and to find them their interests, their tastes, young women that can be manipulated. That person will often describe themselves as a casting director to go out there and to tell the women to come onto the base. Once they're on the base, anything can happen to them. Like I said, they are afforded no protections from their government and our government is not going to prosecute the men that do anything on that base.

verification.notes: The transcript attributes this account to unnamed people contacted by Owens. Searches found documented trafficking and prostitution around some overseas U.S. bases, but no reliable source substantiated the specific recurring method of female recruiters posing as casting directors for senior personnel or the categorical claim that women brought onto bases have no legal protection. Anonymous-source details cannot be corroborated from available evidence.
